We need to return the mapped_rxn associated with the template that, when applied to the molecule, reproduces the described reaction: cycloaddition where two unsaturated parts combine to form a cyclic product, forming C-C bond, breaking C-O, losing ketone and C-C triple bonds functional groups.

We have applied template 1914386 and got two precursors: 'C#C[Si](C)(C)C' and 'COC(=O)C(=O)CCc1ccccc1'. The mapped_rxn for template 1914386 is in its entry: we saw in search result entry for reaction_id 1914386 includes mapped_rxn: '[CH:14]#[C:15][Si:16]([CH3:17])([CH3:18])[CH3:19].O=[C:5]([C:3]([O:2][CH3:1])=[O:4])[CH2:6][CH2:7][c:8]1[cH:9][cH:10][cH:11][cH:12][cH:13]1>>[CH3:1][O:2][C:3](=[O:4])[C:5]1(/[CH:6]=[CH:7]/[c:8]2[cH:9][cH:10][cH:11][cH:12][cH:13]2)[CH:14]=[C:15]1[Si:16]([CH3:17])([CH3:18])[CH3:19]'

We need to return mapped_rxn and template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash). The template_id is 1914386? Actually template_id is integer identifier used to search. In search results, each entry has reaction_id and template_hash. The template_id likely corresponds to reaction_id? The tool get_template expects template_id. We used get_template with 4326 earlier. So template_id is the integer we used to retrieve. For 1914386, we haven't retrieved via get_template but we can assume template_id = 1914386. Let's verify by calling get_template for 1914386.
